claims.claim: Justin Alexander says the delve format artificially isolates the encounter from its context and so defeats its own purpose.
claims.source: Justin Alexander, 'Are We Really This Stupid?', The Alexandrian, 2011
claims.page: Are We Really This Stupid?, 'Isolated Encounters'

claims.claim: Justin Alexander asks publishers to trust DMs rather than pre-programming every monster's behaviour in the text.
claims.source: Justin Alexander, 'Are We Really This Stupid?', The Alexandrian, 2011
claims.quote: publishers can put a little more trust in DMs
claims.page: Are We Really This Stupid?, 'Encounters on the Fly'

claims.claim: Brendan of Necropraxis describes the dominant published format as areas written out in lengthy proper English prose.
claims.quote: Areas are described in lengthy, proper english prose.

claims.claim: Brendan of Necropraxis grants that well-written prose modules are pleasurable to read.
Brendan of Necropraxis says the same prose modules are cumbersome to use in play.
claims.quote: quite cumbersome to use in play

claims.claim: Brendan of Necropraxis objects that Courtney Campbell's outline key, though usable, lacks poetry.
Brendan of Necropraxis keeps running prose but bolds the features the referee needs immediately.
claims.quote: I bold the immediately relevant features.

claims.claim: Brendan of Necropraxis faults boxed text for separating a thing's first impression from its elaboration further down the page.
claims.quote: separated the initial impression (“treasure chest”) from elaboration

claims.claim: Brendan of Necropraxis says the aim of bolding is that the referee can take in the area with a glance.
claims.quote: take in the area with a glance

claims.claim: On his worked example Brendan of Necropraxis reports the text that must be read is cut by more than half without degrading the prose.
claims.quote: cut down by more than half

claims.claim: Reviewing a 2006 DCC module, Gabor Lux says much boxed text and follow-up writing are expended to say relatively little.
claims.source: Gabor Lux (Melan), '[REVIEW] Halls of the Minotaur', Beyond Fomalhaut, 2018
claims.quote: much boxed text and followup writing are expended to say relatively little

claims.claim: Gabor Lux reports that the same module played better at the table than it read on the page.
claims.source: Gabor Lux (Melan), '[REVIEW] Halls of the Minotaur', Beyond Fomalhaut, 2018
claims.quote: It really did play better than it reads

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch's rule in a 2026 review is that read-aloud should never be long.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch says long read-aloud makes players lose focus and reach for their phones.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: Long read-aloud causes players to loose focus

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch says long passages set in italics are cognitively hard to read.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, review of 'The Swan Hollow Intrigue', tenfootpole.org, 2026
claims.quote: Long italics is hard to read, cognitively.
